extracted.intended_audience: readers, instructors, and students using the second edition of the textbook "Analysis" (authors, errata users)
extracted.subtask_description: A collected errata list giving corrections and required assumptions/wording changes for the second edition of the Analysis textbook; intended to correct theorems, proofs, exercises, notation, and references. Use when updating the book or checking correctness of statements/proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 1.4 hypothesis: require ∅ and Ω in A
rubrics_metrics.description: In the hypothesis of Theorem 1.4 it is necessary to require that the set A contains the empty set ∅ and the whole set Ω.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stating hypotheses about a collection A of sets in measure/measure-theory contexts, explicitly require that A contains ∅ and the whole space Ω so that subsequent measure-theoretic operations/arguments are valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent symbol usage in section 1.5 (paragraph 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: In paragraph 6, where essential support is defined, the symbol Ω is incorrectly used (elsewhere Ω denotes the underlying measure space; in this paragraph it denotes a collection of open sets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change the local symbol (in that paragraph only) from Ω to another symbol (e.g., script O) so symbols remain consistent: reserve Ω for the underlying measure space throughout section 1.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name correction: Levi → Beppo Levi
rubrics_metrics.description: Change Levi to Beppo Levi in the penultimate paragraph on page 16.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct historical/mathematical name 'Beppo Levi' where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefine sequences on null sets to be pointwise monotone and integrals unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace second line by: 'for every x in a set Ω ∼ Θ, where Θ ∈ Σ and µ(Θ) = 0. Let us redefine the f_j by setting f_j(x) = 0, for x ∈ Θ, while f_j(x) is unchanged for x ∉ Θ. This redefinition makes the sequence monotone for all x ∈ Ω, but it does not change the integral I_j = ∫ f_j dµ.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dealing with pointwise monotone sequences defined only almost everywhere, redefine values on a µ-null set to get a monotone sequence defined for all x without changing integrals; state this redefinition explicitly at start of proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make functions everywhere defined; treat non-summable f
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete certain lines and replace phrase 'well defined a.e.' by: 'well defined for all x. If µ({x : f(x) = ∞}) > 0 we say that f is not summable for the purpose of the following Theorem 1.6. In any case we set f(x) = 0 on the set {x : f(x) = ∞} so that our new f is a function from Ω → R, in conformity with the definition on the first line of 1.5.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a function takes the value ∞ on a set of positive measure, state the convention (e.g., call it not summable) and set its value arbitrarily (here 0) on points with ∞ to obtain a real-valued function for subsequent arguments; be explicit about such conventions in theorem statements/proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof housekeeping: reference redefined objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Add first line to the proof: 'In the following, f_j and f refer to the sequence and the limit as redefined above.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preceding text redefines functions/objects for technical convenience, begin subsequent proofs by explicitly stating which versions of the objects are in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fubini application requires sigma-finite measure space
rubrics_metrics.description: In Theorem 1.13 one has to assume that the measure space (Ω, Σ, µ) is sigma-finite. Only then can one apply Fubini’s theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying Fubini/Tonelli, include the sigma-finiteness hypothesis on the measure space (unless using a version that removes it); explicitly state this assumption in the theorem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bathtub principle (Theorem 1.14): sigma-finite measure space and uniqueness caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: In Theorem 1.14 (Bathtub principle) the space (Ω, Σ, µ) has to be assumed to be sigma-finite since the proof relies on the layer cake representation. Also add caveat to uniqueness: the assumption needed that the infimum I in (1) be finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State sigma-finiteness and finiteness of the infimum I as hypotheses required for the proof and for uniqueness assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 1.19: correct piecewise definition of g_ε
rubrics_metrics.description: The last displayed equation in the proof of Corollary 1.19 should be changed to the given piecewise definition: g_ε(x) = h_ε(x−a) if x ≤ a+ε; = 1 if a+ε ≤ x ≤ b; = h_ε(b+ε−x) if x ≥ b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the corrected piecewise formula as written; ensure symmetry/transition pieces and cutoffs are correctly specified in mollifier/approximation constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing exponent p on λ(y)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the displayed equation between (4) and (5): replace λ(y) by λ(y)^p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check exponents on weight/measure terms in displayed equations; missing exponent can change the nature of norm/weight computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform boundedness proof for p = ∞ needs sigma-finiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: Our proof of Theorem 2.12 (Uniform boundedness principle) requires that the measure space be sigma-finite for the case p = ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State sigma-finiteness when considering L^∞-type arguments relying on measure decomposition or countable unions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct norm notation after displayed formula
rubrics_metrics.description: The line after the first displayed formula should read kf k and not kf k2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the subscript/notation indicating a norm (and its exponent) is the intended one; typographical misplacement of exponent/subscript can misrepresent which norm is referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 2.23: domain specification
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 2.23 add the sentence: Here, Ω is any Lebesgue measurable subset of R^n of positive measure (which need not contain any ball).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stating exercises involving domains, specify measurability and measure positivity explicitly; do not implicitly require interior balls unless intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layer-cake representation assumptions: monotone → non-decreasing and values at 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace 'two monotone functions' by 'two monotone non-decreasing functions'. Also assume that φ1(0) and φ2(0) are zero so that the layer cake representation Theorem 1.13 holds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking the layer-cake (or similar decomposition) ensure monotonicity is specified as non-decreasing and initial values at 0 are set appropriately for representation formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item (v): require Φ lower semi-continuous; change monotonicity direction
rubrics_metrics.description: In item (v) require the function Φ to be lower semi-continuous since the left side is lower semi-continuous by definition. Also, just before (vi), change 'nonincreasing' to 'nondecreasing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match continuity/semi-continuity hypotheses with the semicontinuity properties of expressions involved; ensure monotonicity direction is consistent across statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula (2): J'_+(t) ≥ 0 ensures expressions defined
rubrics_metrics.description: In equation (2) note that J'_+(t) ≥ 0 and hence all the expressions in formula (2) are properly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out nonnegativity of right-derivative when it guarantees terms (e.g., measures/densities) are nonnegative and expressions are well-defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 3: A and B must be sets of finite measure
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 3 A and B should be sets of finite measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly require finite measure of sets when integrability or measure-based conclusions depend on finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct ordering/format of norm-product expression
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last line of equation (13) replace kgkqkhkr by the corrected ordering/format (originally misprinted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure product of norms is written with correct placement of exponents/subscripts (e.g., ||g||_q ||h||_r) to avoid ambiguity; correct typographical errors in norm notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence remark: point reader to Exercise 2 (page 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: After formula (5) it is mentioned that (3) and (5) are equivalent. The meaning of this statement is explained in Exercise 2 on page 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting equivalence of forms, reference the explicit exercise or proof that clarifies the equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement about conformal maps: dimension and regularity assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The paragraph that begins 'It is a theorem ...' should read: 'For n ≥ 3, and for sufficiently regular transformations (C^4 will do), it is a theorem ...'. Add: 'For n = 2 the conformal maps are analytic functions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State dimension assumptions (n≥3) and required regularity (e.g., C^4) for geometric-analytic theorems; separately note the n=2 (complex-analytic) case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.2: change p to q
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 4.2 change p to q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix typographical variable mismatches to reflect intended exponents/parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 4.4: require λ > 0
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 4.4 one has to assume that λ > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add positivity hypotheses on parameters when proofs or statements rely on them (e.g., to avoid sign/pathologies).

rubrics_metrics.name: 5.3(4): replace (x − y)2 by |x − y|^2
rubrics_metrics.description: In 5.3(4) and the following equation, change (x − y)2 to |x − y|^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use absolute-value squared when referring to squared Euclidean distance; correct ambiguous or incorrect typographical superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark: delete stray phrase about Green's function
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the words 'and for the Green’s function of the Laplacian (before 6.20)' in the Remark at the top of page 132.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove incorrect or misleading parenthetical phrases from remarks to keep statements accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summation index correction near Section 6.9
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lines before Section 6.9, the summation should be j = 1 to m and not j = 1 to n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure summation index ranges are correct and correspond to intended finite sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend local validity to whole test function space (6.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the first sentence of 6.16 add: If (1) holds in D(O) then it holds for functions in D(Ω) that have support in O, and hence it holds for the whole of D(Ω). On page 151 (4), and the line before, replace Ω by O.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When statements are first proved on a subdomain O, explicitly indicate how they extend to test functions supported in O and then to the whole space via density/partition of unity arguments; correct variable usage (O vs Ω).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove accidental square on gradient norm
rubrics_metrics.description: In the top displayed equation, replace |∇f(x)|^2 by |∇f(x)|, i.e., remove the square from the right side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether squared norms or plain norms are intended in displayed estimates; correct typographical power errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing parenthesis before ∂G_y
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last equation there should be a '(' before '∂G_y'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix missing parentheses that affect differentiation/integration boundary notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm exponent correction in displayed equation (page 175)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first displayed equation replace kf − gmk by kf − gmk^2 (i.e., include square on the appropriate norm indicator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct norm exponent/subscript typos to reflect intended squared-norm statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong limit existence for L^p: p < ∞
rubrics_metrics.description: In the middle of the page, the strong limit exists in L^p for p < ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the correct Lebesgue exponent range when asserting existence of strong limits; avoid overstating existence for p=∞ when it only holds for p<∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace measure µ by ν in kernel formula
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second displayed formula replace µ by ν, i.e., the formula should read K_ν(z) ≈ ... (with ν in place of µ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the correct measure symbol is used in kernel/transform formulas; inconsistent measure names change meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delete erroneous limit sign in formula (1) on page 184
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete the limit sign in formula (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove stray limit notation that does not belong in formulas and could change the expression's meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 7.17: clarify hypothesis and proof start (f→0, not assuming f ∈ L^2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentence in the hypothesis of Theorem 7.17 should read: 'We define (f, |p|f ) here to be given by Eq. 7.12(4). We assume that f goes to 0 at ∞, but it is not assumed that f ∈ L^2(R^n).' The proof should start: 'Without loss of generality we can replace f by |f|, which does not change f* or |∇f| and only decreases (f, |p|f ) in 7.12(4). Thus, we assume, henceforth, that f ≥ 0. We also take 1 > c > 0 in part 1.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State decay-at-infinity assumptions separate from L^2 membership and begin proofs by reducing to nonnegative functions when symmetrical rearrangements/absolute-value-preserving operations are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide completed proof for strictness when f ∉ L^2
rubrics_metrics.description: The assertion of the strictness of inequality (2) was not fully proved for f ∉ L^2. Provide the additional argument using the quadratic form Q and the functions g=(f−c)+, h=f−g, show Q(g,h)/2 = A−B, note I<∞ for g, use Theorem 3.9 and conclude equality only when g=g* and h=h* up to translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an argument relies on approximation steps that might lose strictness in a limit, include an alternate direct argument (e.g., via quadratic forms and rearrangement inequalities) to preserve strictness under the weaker hypothesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetic-gradient term sign correction
rubrics_metrics.description: In the displayed equation in the middle of the page just above 'and hence', replace '-i' in the rightmost term by '+', i.e., it should read χ_m(∇ + iA)f + (∇χ_m)f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix sign errors in complex/magnetic gradient expressions; sign determines gauge/phase and is critical in operator identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 7: inequality direction correction
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 7 the inequality is in the wrong direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reverse the inequality where appropriate; small sign/direction errors change the intended claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 8.3: absolute value around (x − a)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the expression on the last line of the statement of Theorem 8.3, (x − a) should be |x − a|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use absolute value when referring to distances; parentheses without absolute value can be ambiguous or incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gamma function argument correction in Equation (4)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Equation (4) replace Γ(n − 1) by Γ(N/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure gamma-function arguments/parameters match dimension/constants used elsewhere; typographical mismatches can produce incorrect constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower limit correction in integral
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last integral of the second displayed equation: the lower limit should be a and not x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check integration limits carefully; wrong limits invalidate integral identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality sign correction for x_n
rubrics_metrics.description: The inequality 0 < x_n < |x| cos(θ) in the second displayed expression is incorrect. It should be replaced by x_n > |x| cos(θ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct direction/placement of geometric inequalities relating components and norms; ensure the inequality reflects the intended geometric relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 8.9(iii): supremum domain must be ω (open bounded subset of Ω)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem 8.9 (iii) is not correct as written. The supremum has to be taken in ω which is an open bounded subset of Ω. In the last line replace sup_{x∈Ω} by sup_{x∈ω}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suprema are taken, ensure the correct domain (e.g., a bounded open subset ω) is specified for compactness/attainment properties; global sup over Ω may be incorrect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify definition of g_j and use essential support
rubrics_metrics.description: In the second paragraph the definition g_j = (f_j − ε/2)+ is correct but complicated. It suffices to define g_j = f_j ≥ 0. At the bottom of page 216 replace H^1_0 (twice) by W^{1,p}_0. On the top of page 216 replace 'support' by 'essential support' (since f_j is not assumed to be continuous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simpler auxiliary function choices when possible; use the correct Sobolev space notation W^{1,p}_0 and use 'essential support' rather than 'support' when functions need not be continuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographical correction to g_α reference
rubrics_metrics.description: In the line after equation (2) replace gα by the correctly formatted g_α (fix typographical subscript).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subscripts/superscripts are correctly typeset to reflect intended indexed families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 8.11: include p = 1 case but proof must be adjusted
rubrics_metrics.description: In Theorem 8.11 the case p = 1 is included in the statement. The Theorem as it stands is correct, but the proof given does not work in the case p = 1 since Theorem 2.18 requires p > 1. To prove the Theorem for p = 1, proceed as before but use q > 1 (any number less than n/(n − 1)), apply Theorem 2.18 to obtain a weak limit in L^q, show gradient zero in distributional sense and conclude constant, then use compact embedding to get contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extending results to endpoint exponents (p=1), verify that supporting theorems used in the proof do not require strict inequality p>1; if they do, adapt the argument using intermediate q>1 and compactness/weak convergence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nash inequality constant corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: The constant in Nash’s inequality is not correct. The previously printed factor should be replaced by the corrected factor (replacement specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify constants in functional inequalities (Nash, Sobolev, etc.); small numeric/functional-constant errors need correction because they affect sharpness and subsequent estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical reference date correction for Stam
rubrics_metrics.description: In paragraph 4 replace 'middle seventies by [Stam]' by 'late fifties by [Stam]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct historical dating/attribution of results in bibliographic comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling correction: Yosida (remove stray 'h')
rubrics_metrics.description: After equation (3) remove the 'h' from Yoshida. It should read Yosida (but note that the 'si' is pronounced 'shi').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct author name spellings in text and bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable-exponent norm and parameter corrections (8.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Equation (2) of 8.18 and in the second displayed equation on page 233 replace k g_t k_{p(t)} by k g_t k_{p(t)−1} (and other exponent/parameter corrections). In the sixth line of page 233 replace a by a^2 (i.e., a = ... should be a^2 = ...). In Equation (4) on page 233 replace kgT k_∞ by the corrected norm expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-check norm exponents and parameter formulas in variable-exponent spaces; correct exponents/coefficient algebraic mistakes to maintain consistency with definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 1 (p.235): domain assumptions for Sobolev-space assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise 1 is not correctly stated: considering three dimensions and domain Ω = R^3 \{0"}, removing one point does not change the Sobolev space, i.e., H^1_0(Ω) = H^1(R^3), so the second assertion is not correct. If one changes the problem by considering open and bounded sets then the second assertion is true. In fact it suffices to consider sets Ω whose complement is a set of positive capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing counterexamples/exercises about Sobolev spaces, specify domain hypotheses (e.g., boundedness or positive-capacity complement) clearly; removing a single point from R^n may not change H^1 spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to which displayed equation contains equalities (page 240)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the third line replace 'in (2) become equalities' by 'in (3) become equalities'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix cross-references to the correct numbered displayed equations to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green-potential constant: add overall factor
rubrics_metrics.description: The right side of equation (5) should have an overall factor [(n − 2)|S^{n−1}|]^{-1}, i.e., V(x) = [(n − 2)|S^{n−1}|]^{-1} * ( ... ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include correct dimensional/normalizing constants in fundamental solution/potential formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise 5(a): remove redundant measurability instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: In Exercise 5(a) delete the sentence 'You have to show ...'. (The measurability is trivial.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid including unnecessary hints or directions that state trivialities and may confuse readers; remove redundant instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity/differentiability statement: Kf vs Kf1 and domain B1
rubrics_metrics.description: Four lines after equation (4) replace '... Kf2 and Kf1 have the same continuity and differentiability properties.' by '... Kf and Kf1 have the same continuity and differentiability properties in B1.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fix function names and specify the domain (e.g., B1) where properties hold; correct typographical errors in function labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit notation correction: j ⇀ ∞ → j → ∞
rubrics_metrics.description: In the limit sign in the last displayed equation on the page replace j ⇀ ∞ by j → ∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate arrow notation: ⇀ denotes weak convergence; → denotes usual (strong) limit. Use them correctly according to context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign correction in displayed equation (page 271) and example potential fix
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first displayed equation change minus '−' to plus '+'. In line 3, the potential −|x|^{-3} is a bad example since it is not locally integrable; the potential −|x|^{-5/2} will do the trick since the kinetic energy scales with λ^2 and the potential scales with λ^{5/2}, driving the energy to −∞.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct arithmetic/ sign errors in displayed formulas; when giving counterexamples ensure the potential is locally integrable and scales correctly to illustrate the intended phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute-value on inner product with potential
rubrics_metrics.description: In equation (6) change (ψ, V ψ) to |(ψ, V ψ)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use absolute-value notation when the magnitude is intended rather than signed inner product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline proof of 11.4: remove unnecessary subsequence step
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof of 11.4 is correct but can be streamlined. In the last line of p.274 delete 'for a sequence of ψ_j's,'. On the top of p.275, delete 'there is a subsequence .... such that'. The ψ_j converge weakly by assumption and Theorem 8.6 states strong convergence for the whole sequence. There is no need to pass to a subsequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary subsequence extraction when a whole-sequence convergence theorem is applicable; simplify proofs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace C_0^∞ by C_c^∞ in Remark (2)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Remark (2) replace C^∞_0 by C^∞_c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct notation for test function spaces: C_c^∞ denotes infinitely differentiable functions with compact support; C^∞_0 is ambiguous/less standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording tweak: 'follows the lines of the integration by parts argument'
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last paragraph 'follows the integration by parts argument ...' should read 'follows the lines of the integration by parts argument ...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise phrasing to indicate that an argument follows an established line of reasoning rather than exactly the same steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive vs strictly positive: use earlier definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the end of the first paragraph from 'strictly positive for all x ∈ R^n' to 'positive as in the definition in Remark (1) after the statement of Theorem 7.8 (Convexity inequality for gradients)'. Similarly replace 'strictly positive' by 'positive as in the definition in Remark (1)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the book's earlier precise notion of 'positive' rather than informal 'strictly positive' when referring back to a prior definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness proof clarification for minimizer ψ_0 in Theorem 11.8
rubrics_metrics.description: The proof that ψ_0 in Theorem 11.8 is unique is not clearly stated. If ψ_0 and φ_0 are minimizers then their real and imaginary parts are minimizers, so assume both are real. Then form the minimizer χ_0 = ψ_0 + iφ_0 and use prior results to see that ψ_0 = c φ_0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proving uniqueness among minimizers, reduce to real-valued cases and use linear combinations and previously proved uniqueness results to deduce proportionality/uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Min-max principle: normalize test function φ
rubrics_metrics.description: In the third version of the min-max principle, the function φ appearing in formula (5) should be normalized, (φ, φ) = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include normalization conditions (unit norm) for variational characterizations to avoid scaling ambiguities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equation (4) condition: n ≥ 3 (not n = 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equation (4) should read n ≥ 3 instead of n = 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct inequalities/assumptions on dimension indices to reflect the range where the statement holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace G^- by G_R
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace G^- by G_R in the first displayed equation on page 318.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the intended Green-function notation consistently (e.g., G_R for Dirichlet Green function on a ball of radius R) instead of stray superscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing square in spectral expression (Thm 12.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Eq. (2) in Thm. 12.9 a square is missing on the left side, namely |ψ(k, y)|^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure powers/squares are present in L^2-norm or density expressions where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography author initial correction: Simon B
rubrics_metrics.description: Change reference 'Reed, M. and Simon, N.' to 'Reed, M. and Simon, B.'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct initials/author names in bibliography entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography ordering correction for Hermann Weyl
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference to Hermann Weyl is not in alphabetical order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bibliography entries are alphabetized correctly (by author surname) according to the chosen style.
